text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
DAWN
- South Asian leaders may allow political dialogue within their seven-nation bloc, ending a ban on discussion of such matters, a Maldivian government minister said.
- South Asian leaders have agreed to speed up dismantling trade barriers within the region and conclude a free trade area agreement early, Indian Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral said.
- The Punjab provincial government has decided to withdraw exemptions of property tax on all government buildings.
- One person was killed and 11 injured by an earthquake which jolted parts of Punjab, North West Frontier province and Pakistan-held Kashmir.
- Pakistan and Sri Lanka have agreed to boost bilateral trade, establish joint ventures and revive a joint economic commission, Sri Lanka's trade minister said in Male.
- Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif said he was confident India would agree to discuss the future of divided Kashmir in bilateral talks and urged India to withdraw troops from the Himalayan region.
- Pakistan has attained self-reliance in its nuclear programme and is in a position to continue and extend its programme for peaceful purposes, said Pakistani scientist Dr Qadeer Khan.
- Three major Japanese securities banks have told Finance Minister Sartaj Aziz they are ready to float samurai bonds worth $500 million in Japan to raise foreign exchange for Pakistan.

- The new economic strategy aiming at five percent growth in agriculture, seven percent in manufacturing and 15 percent in exports would place the economy on the historic growth path of six percent in the next fiscal year, said Deputy Chairman Planning Commission Dr Hafeez Pasha.
- A high-powered 27-member South Korean trade delegation will arrive Karachi on May 17 on a four-day visit to discuss increased bilateral cooperation specially trade relations.
BUSINESS RECORDER
- The sales tax net is likely to be widened in the next budget scheduled to be announced in June, sources said.
- Sindh province will be facing a shortfall of 1.6 million tonnes of wheat this year, an official said.
- Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif arrived in Ashgabat for a two-day visit to attend the extraordinary summit of the Economic Cooperation Organisation.
- Two power plants with a total capacity of 335 MW are expected to be commissioned by September.
THE NEWS
- The Federal Investigation Agency arrested six officials of Schon Group and National Fibers Lt on fraud charges.
- Commerce Minister Ishaq Dar informed the Senate that a report on the Mehran Bank scandal, exonerating President Farooq Leghari, was missing from the official records.
- President Farooq Leghari will pay a three-day visit to United Arab Emirates by the end of May.
- A seven-member delegation led by the Secretary at the Defence Ministry left for Britain for the second meeting of the Pak-UK Defence Cooperation Forum meeting.
THE NATION
- Pakistan People's Party leader Benazir Bhutto denied reports that she was seeking asylum in Britain.
- District Administration Jhang has imposed a curfew in parts of the city during the Moslem mourning month of Muharram.
- Six persons, including five from the same family, were killed and two injured by a soldier in two separate incidents in Sargodha, in northern Punjab province.
THE MUSLIM
- Interior Minister Chaudhry Shujaat Hussain ruled out the involvement of foreign elements in recent sectarian violence.
- The Ehtesab (accountability) Commission has finalised cases against serving and retired chairmen of the Pakistan National Institute of Health.
- The Pakistan Muslim League won another seat in the provincial assembly of Balochistan in a by-election held in provincial constituency PB-34 Lasbela-I.
-- Islamabad newsroom 9251-274757
